paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jesus is teaching His disciples how to treat people, and it starts with a warning: "It is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the one through whom they come!" (Luke 17:1). So He tells them, "Watch yourselves." (Luke 17:3). That one is heavy, and it means we are responsible for how we treat the people around us, especially "these little ones" (Luke 17:2).

Then Jesus gets to forgiveness, and He doesn't leave much wiggle room. "If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him." (Luke 17:3). Even seven times in a day, you must forgive him (Luke 17:4). The apostles hear that and say, "Increase our faith!" (Luke 17:5). I think I would have said the same thing, and louder, with my mustache flapping.

Jesus answers with a mustard seed of faith and a servant who simply does his duty (Luke 17:6-10). I think the point is that forgiving again and again isn't about having a giant pile of faith. It's about doing what the Lord has commanded, without keeping score or waiting for applause. So when you've done it all, you say, "We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty." (Luke 17:10). Go forgive, friend, and let the Lord handle the rest.
